_note: THE INDUSTRIAL FAMILY, 6 OF 10: THE NIGHT SHIFT.
One worker hid when the occupiers came and has been hiding since. Clear the floor, find her, and then do the one
thing she asks: clock her out at the door, because she has not been paid for any of this. The verb is FIND, and the
end is a joke she means completely.
Industrial dungeons (LocTypeDungeon_ThemeIndustrial, 20 per Eliza's count), vanilla interiors that carry the
delve markers today. Every word holds in any of them: nothing names the site, the faction or what the plant
made; everything a line points at is placed. Pay: med, capped.

place._theme: Industrial dungeons; the delve marker set.

prose.name: Rescue: Night Shift on <Planet>
prose.briefing: One worker on the night shift hid when the <Place> was taken. She's still in there.
prose.card: Local Contract. See the night-shift worker out of the <Place> on <Planet>. Payment on contract completion.

beats.journal: Whoever led the occupiers is dead. Now I need to find the night-shift worker somewhere inside.
say: It's quiet. Come and find me, and say something friendly first.

beats.journal: The night-shift worker had been hiding in the <Place> since it was taken. She won't leave until she's clocked out, so I need to clock her out on the way out.

person.name: Dot Ferreira
hellos: If you're one of them, I'm not here.

greeting: Oh, you're not one of them. Thank goodness. I've been hiding since my shift started, and nobody has clocked me out.

reply: Yes. But clock me out on the way out. I've been on shift for days, and I want it on the record.
I'm the night shift. Nobody ever sees the night shift. That's been a problem my whole career, and this week it was very useful.
Everybody's lunch. I'll be leaving some notes of apology.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 ends the talk and sets the next stage. Voice 'Cat, Droll and Dry', unused so far.

beats.objective: Clock her out at the shift clock

message.title: Shift Clock
message.text: Clocked in: the night the place was taken. Clocked out: now.

beats.journal: I clocked the night-shift worker out of the <Place>. It's on the record now, every hour of it.
beats.name: Shift Clock
say: It took. I'd like that framed.

broadcast: Is someone there? Don't answer if you're one of them. I'm still inside. I'll come out when it's quiet, and not before.
_speech: On a board the broadcast waits for him at the site. Not yet heard in game; his ear decides. No names, places, factions or currency in a voiced line.
